key_insight: Replacing antithetic reflection pairs with equally spaced complex-circle samples stabilizes Gaussian-smoothing estimates of high-order derivatives as the step size shrinks.
engineering_relevance: The estimator offers an alternative to costly high-order automatic differentiation for PINNs solving high-order partial differential equations.
method: Estimate derivatives using Stein’s identity and Gaussian smoothing.
Extend antithetic sampling to n equally spaced points on a circle in the complex plane.
Under local analyticity and n at least the derivative order, obtain O(σ^n) bias and bounded variance as σ approaches zero.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate effectiveness in PINNs for polyharmonic and Cahn–Hilliard equations.
watch_item: The guarantees require local analyticity, and implementation requires evaluating the target function at complex-valued inputs.
paper_title: Variance Stable Gaussian Smoothing Estimator for Arbitrary High-order Derivatives
